Case: Ramiro is a 63-year-old with history of renal cell carcinoma who presents with acute neck and arm pain. Ramiro says he has had neck discomfort for several weeks, but It suddenly became worse this morning, when he had an episode of electrical pain shooting down his arms and back . Ramiro endorses severe pain that is worse with flexion and extension of his neck and denies any recent trauma. In attempts to control the pain he has tried ibuprofen and acetaminophen with no relief. On physical examination, you note that he is very tender to palpation of his cervical spine and that flexion of the neck elicits severe shooting pains down his spine. MRI of the cervical spine shows multifocal lesions throughout his cervical spine, with pathologic fracture of C4 and canal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer Ramiro intravenous hydromorphone for pain control? Yes or no? If yes, what dose – Low (0.5 mg), or High (1 mg)? Explain.
